screen1.title: HOW ERP WORKS
screen1.subtitle: ERP helps people with OCD practice facing what triggers them while changing what they do next.
screen1.quote: “You don't practice being fearless. You practice responding differently.”

screen2.title: You've Just Left the House.
screen2.urge_tag: You feel the urge to go back
screen2.subtitle: A common moment of doubt arrives. Let's see what happens when the urge is followed.

screen3.title: Follow the Urge
screen3.checking_status: Checking the handle... turning the key...
screen3.doubt_thought: “Wait... did I really lock it properly?”
screen3.subtitle: The relief settled the feeling for a second, but doubt returned right after.

screen4.title: What Did the Check Give You?
screen4.point2: More reason to check again when doubt returns.
screen4.subtitle: Checking can reduce distress in the moment, but that short-term relief reinforces the brain's urge to check again.

screen5.title: Let's Try the Same Moment Differently.
screen5.urge_tag: The urge appears: “Go back and check”
screen5.subtitle: This time, instead of automatically following the urge, we explore the ERP approach.

screen6.title: 1. Exposure
screen6.subtitle1: ERP starts by approaching a trigger rather than avoiding it or making it go away.
screen6.thought: “The doubt is here: Did I lock the door?”
screen6.subtitle2: In ERP, exposure means allowing the trigger or uncertainty to be present without immediately trying to push it out of mind.

screen7.title: 2. Response Prevention
screen7.subtitle1: Then comes the second part: resisting or delaying the compulsive response.
screen7.thought: Urge: “Go back and check right now.”
screen7.subtitle2: Simulated practice: Choosing not to perform the ritual gives the brain a chance to learn something new.

screen9.title: The Point Isn't to Feel Nothing.
screen9.subtitle: ERP is not about making distress disappear instantly. It teaches:
screen9.insight1: “I can experience uncertainty and tolerate it.”
screen9.insight2: “I can have an urge without automatically acting on it.”
screen9.insight3: “I don't need a ritual to respond to every doubt.”

screen10.title: You Sent an Important Message.
screen10.question: What would response prevention look like?
screen10.opt_read: Read the message again to be sure
screen10.opt_ask: Ask someone if it sounds okay
screen10.opt_leave: Leave it as it is for now without re-reading
screen10.feedback_correct: ✓ That's an example of resisting the checking or reassurance response.
screen10.feedback_incorrect: That would be a way of responding to the uncertainty. In ERP, response prevention means practicing not using the checking or reassurance behavior.

screen11.title: ERP Changes What You Do Next.
screen11.subtitle: The goal isn't to eliminate every intrusive thought or feeling. It's to build a different response to them.
